title: The Wolf and the Fox (हिन्दी)

full_text:
In a rocky gorge lived a powerful, tyrannical wolf who forced a clever fox to be his servant. Whenever the fox caught a hare or found a wild honeycomb, the wolf would snarl, bare his fangs, and snatch the prize, leaving the fox only bones and bitter roots. The fox endured the humiliation patiently, waiting for an opportunity to liberate himself from the tyrant’s yoke.

One autumn afternoon, as the wolf rested under a pomegranate tree, his stomach rumbled with insatiable hunger. He kicked the fox and growled: 'Go into the valley and fetch me fat meat, or I shall devour you before nightfall!'

The fox bowed meekly and ran toward the village. In the orchard of an affluent farmer, he discovered a deep pit dug by the peasants to catch wild boars. The pit was covered with slender reeds and concealed with fresh green turf, with a savory roasted kid placed in the center as bait.

Returning to the wolf, the fox whispered with breathless excitement: 'Rejoice, O mighty master! In the orchard below lies a roasted kid so tender that the grease drips from its ribs, guarded by neither dog nor man! Because of my loyalty to you, I did not touch a morsel, leaving the feast for your royal jaws.'

The greedy wolf leaped to his feet, saliva dripping from his jowls. Without pausing to examine the ground, he galloped into the orchard and leaped straight toward the roasted kid. The fragile reeds snapped under his heavy weight, and the wolf crashed down into the bottom of the deep pit, trapped between sheer walls of stone.

The wolf howled in terror and pleaded: 'Help me out, faithful companion! Throw down a rope or call the other beasts to pull me up!'

The fox stood safely at the lip of the pit, looked down with a calm smile, and said: 'For three years you bullied the weak, stole their sustenance, and threatened their lives. Now learn that he who builds his kingdom on terror will find that his own greed digs the pit of his downfall.' The fox trotted merrily away into the woods, free at last, while the village watchmen arrived to secure the captured beast.
moral: Tyranny and bullying provoke subtle wit, and the arrogant oppressor is ultimately trapped by his own greed. [HI]
